stem: Which of the following graphical tools is most appropriate for displaying the cumulative frequency of a grouped frequency distribution?

per_option_rationale.rationale: A histogram shows class frequencies as bar heights, not cumulative frequencies.
A frequency polygon connects midpoints of class frequencies; it does not plot cumulative values.
An ogive (cumulative frequency curve) is specifically constructed by plotting cumulative frequency against upper class boundaries.
A pie chart shows proportional composition of a total; it is not used for cumulative frequency.

explanation: An ogive is the graph of cumulative frequency against class boundaries. It is the standard tool for reading off medians, quartiles, and percentiles graphically from a frequency distribution.

explanation_sections.punchline: Cumulative frequency is displayed by an ogive, not a histogram or polygon.
explanation_sections.approach: Match each chart type to its purpose: histogram = frequencies, polygon = shape of distribution, ogive = cumulative, pie = composition.
explanation_sections.lesson: Ogive plots cumulative frequency; it is the only one of the standard four that accumulates.
explanation_sections.timing: 45 s. Direct recall item; verify by the definition of each diagram.
